items.proposed: As SERVER without its signed TCP listener; I06 read connection allowed. For I01 only, an AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET listener (HS53): `bind` and `listen`, and `accept4` only with flags 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC, or SOCK_CLOEXEC with SOCK_NONBLOCK, judged on the low 32 bits of the argument because the kernel reads it as an `int` (O-SECCOMP-V5-OBSERVER-LISTENER). Seccomp sees only a descriptor, so it cannot tell the I01 socket from the observer's TCP sockets (the I06 read connection): `bind` and `listen` reach those too, and the TCP-listen boundary is SELinux's (O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP, O-T04-HS53; residual R-OBSERVER-TCP-LISTEN). The socket's 0700 directory, its 0600 mode and a fresh path at each start come from the observer's unit, not from further calls (O-W03-OBSERVER-UNIT) | `planeon_observer_t`: `name_connect` to `planeon_kubeapi_port_t`; read-only to policy credential; the I01 listener: `create`, `bind`, `listen` and `accept` on its own `unix_stream_socket` (an AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET socket is checked in that class), socket file `planeon_observer_sock_t`, the server its only connector (SELinux matrix v5, `architecture/selinux-matrix-v3/`); no `tcp_socket` `listen` and no `node_bind` (O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP; a later matrix revision closes them in data, O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP) |
items.why: I01 has the server connect to the observer (base §3), and matrix v5 already makes planeon_observer_t that socket's listener, but the row gave the observer no listener, which W01 says blocks implementation rather than being added quietly. The row now grants the I01 listener with the accept4 flags limited, states that the filter cannot refuse a TCP listen, which SELinux must, and puts the socket's directory, mode and freshness on the unit.

## 13. Amendment HS53 (2026-10-17)

HS53 lets the observer hold the one listener I01 needs (§5.3 OBSERVER row) and records who produces I01 (§4.3); the
observer's filter admits the listener only once O-SECCOMP-V5-OBSERVER-LISTENER lands. It is applied to the HS43
effective text, which stays byte-identical; `architecture/host-interface-amendment-hs53/amendment.json` gives every
change and its reason.

| Item | Where | Decisions |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | 5.3 OBSERVER row, seccomp and SELinux | Q-SOL-1, Q-SOL-2, Q-SOL-3, F-SOL-1 |
| H2 | 5.3 text after the table | Q-SOL-1 |
| H3 | 4.3 | Q-SOL-4, F-SOL-1 |

Adopted text HS53 overrides (each file stays byte-identical; HS53 governs, and a successor of that contract adopts it):

| Superseded clause | In | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| "Existing fixed native observer, read-only to policy" | `architecture/host-interface-inputs/corrected/HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md` | a fixed native observer, read-only to policy, whose I01 producer is R10's HE-004-I01 (obligation I01-1 of W03-PLAN-AMEND-2, MET-ENFORCE-032, main c69e55f; W01 §4.3 as amended by HS53) (H3) |
| "The producer is an external operator prerequisite" | `docs/alpha-2/POLICY_OBSERVATION_READINESS.md` | for I01, the producer is R10's HE-004-I01 (obligation I01-1 of W03-PLAN-AMEND-2, MET-ENFORCE-032, main c69e55f; W01 §4.3 as amended by HS53); this guide's protocol, path, modes, framing, limits and peer checks are unchanged (H3) |
| "PREEXISTING_INDEPENDENTLY_INSTALLED_OPEN_SOURCE_PRODUCER" | `architecture/policy-observation-amendment.json` | the operator prerequisite of this channel record: for I01, the observer is produced by R10's HE-004-I01 (obligation I01-1 of W03-PLAN-AMEND-2, MET-ENFORCE-032, main c69e55f; W01 §4.3 as amended by HS53); the record's other fields are unchanged (H3) |
| "as SERVER without the listener; the I06 read connection (connect)" | `architecture/seccomp-allowlists/README.md` | as SERVER without its signed TCP listener; the I06 read connection (connect); and, in seccomp v5, the I01 listener of W01 §5.3 as amended by HS53 (bind, listen, and accept4 with flags 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC or SOCK_CLOEXEC\|SOCK_NONBLOCK) (H1) |

Stated residuals:

- R-OBSERVER-TCP-LISTEN: The observer's filter admits bind and listen on every descriptor it holds, its TCP sockets (the I06 read connection) included, because seccomp sees only the descriptor. Unless the host policy denies planeon_observer_t tcp_socket listen and node_bind, a TCP listener by the observer is refused only where SELinux checks name_bind, which it does not for port 0 or for ports inside ip_local_port_range. Follow-up: obligations O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP and O-T04-HS53, then O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP in data (Q-SOL-2).

The data follow in order (Q-SOL-1 (a)): the W02d allowlist successor (`architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v5/`) gains
the OBSERVER I01 listener rule in the same packet as this amendment, then the OBSERVER programs and the edge record
are republished, then R10's HE-004-I01 re-vendors them and serves I01.

Obligations: O-SECCOMP-V5-OBSERVER-LISTENER (the allowlist rule), O-W03-OBSERVER-UNIT (the socket's directory, mode and freshness), O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP (no TCP listener for the observer), O-T04-HS53 (native confirmation), O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP (the observer's TCP listen closed in data), O-PROGRAMS-V3-OBSERVER (the OBSERVER programs and the edge record), O-R10-HE004-I01 (the observer serves I01). Every E01-E12 obligation stays OPEN_UNPROVEN.

dispositions.summary: Two packets: this amendment with seccomp v5, then the OBSERVER programs and the edge record; the stale W02 data pointer names the current successor (H2).
bind and listen unconditional, accept4 with three flag values; the TCP-listen boundary is SELinux's, in W03's policy, T04's check and a later matrix revision; residual R-OBSERVER-TCP-LISTEN.
The socket's directory, mode and freshness come from the observer's unit, with no new call.
The v1 peer duties stay; HE-004-I01's design decides on HS43's race-free start-time reference.
I01's producer is R10's HE-004-I01; the earlier external-prerequisite statements are superseded for I01.

obligations.label: the allowlist rule
obligations.owner: the W02d allowlist successor v5 (architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v5/), in the same packet as HS53 (Q-SOL-1 (a))
obligations.text: Add to the OBSERVER row of the W02d allowlists, for x86_64 and aarch64, one duty citing HS53's §5.3 OBSERVER row: bind and listen unconditional, and accept4 only when the low 32 bits of argument 3 equal 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC (0x80000) or SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK (0x80800), so SOCK_NONBLOCK alone and every other bit are killed. Keep the runtime bases and every other role unchanged, and replay the v4 vectors: only OBSERVER's bind, listen and accept4 decisions may change, from KILL_PROCESS to ALLOW.

obligations.label: the socket's directory, mode and freshness
obligations.text: Start the observer from a unit that gives I01's socket its required directory and mode without new calls (Q-SOL-3 (a)): RuntimeDirectory= with mode 0700, root:root, for /run/planeon/live-proxy; UMask=0177, so the socket that bind creates is root:root 0600; no socket activation (native profile v3 forbids sockets created elsewhere); and a fresh bind at each start. The directory also holds I02's capacity-broker.sock, so no unit's stop or restart may remove another listener's live socket, and a stale observer socket path must be gone before the observer binds, cleared by something that runs outside the observer's filter. The observer itself adds no umask, fchmod, fchmodat or unlinkat call.

obligations.label: no TCP listener for the observer
obligations.text: Give planeon_observer_t no tcp_socket listen and no node_bind (name_bind is already closed by matrix v5), so a bind or listen that the observer's filter admits on a TCP socket is refused by SELinux, including on port 0 and on ports inside ip_local_port_range, where name_bind is not checked (Q-SOL-2 (a)).

obligations.label: native confirmation
obligations.text: On the enrolled kernel and policy, confirm: the observer's installed filter is the v5 OBSERVER program; accept4 on the I01 socket with flags 0, SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK succeeds, and with SOCK_NONBLOCK alone kills the observer; an AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET socket is checked in the unix_stream_socket class (the author's reading of v6.12 socket_type_to_security_class); the installed policy gives planeon_observer_t no tcp_socket listen and no node_bind, and a TCP listen by the observer is refused; the socket's directory is root:root 0700 and the socket root:root 0600, no socket activation is used, neither unit's stop or restart removes the other listener's live socket, and no stale path is left before a bind.

obligations.label: the observer's TCP listen closed in data
obligations.owner: the next SELinux matrix revision after matrix v6 (matrix v6 stays frozen, Q-SOL-2 (a))
obligations.text: Add tcp_socket listen and node_bind to the matrix's closed permissions for planeon_observer_t, with an assertion that the observer holds neither, so the boundary O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP sets in host policy is also checked in data.

obligations.label: the OBSERVER programs and the edge record
obligations.owner: the parallel lane's next harness-onion packet (packet 2 of SECCOMP-OBSERVER-LISTENER, Q-SOL-1 (a))
obligations.text: Republish the OBSERVER's two compiled programs (x86_64 and aarch64) from seccomp v5 and the edge record that binds them for HE-004, as PROGRAMS-REPUBLISH did for EFFECT_GATE; no other role's program changes, and the edge record takes the next free version.

obligations.label: the observer serves I01
obligations.owner: R10's HE-004-I01 (primary lane; obligation I01-1 of W03-PLAN-AMEND-2)
obligations.text: Re-vendor the republished OBSERVER programs, install them as the observer's filter, and serve I01 on its fixed path with the v1 peer duties in both directions; decide whether HS43's race-free start-time reference applies to I01 and record the choice (Q-SOL-4 (a)).
